newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No damaging cold this week for Brazil coffee-Somar.
newsitem.headline: No damaging cold this week for Brazil coffee-Somar.

text.p: Brazil's coffee regions should see no damaging cold over the coming five days with minimum temperatures this weekend holding above 10 degrees Celsius, local meteorologists Somar said Sunday.
A cold front, which has brought rains throughout the coffee regions, is continuing to prevent an accompanying polar air mass from entering coffee growing areas.
The cold front is expected to bring further rains this week for Parana and south Sao Paulo states, said Somar forecaster Marcio Custodio.

The polar air mass will move out to the ocean but another air mass currently of 1,026 millibars may enter coffee regions during the weekend of July 5/6 which could lead to cooler temperatures in Parana. For the time being no frost is forecast however, Custodio said.
The current wave of air masses have broken off from a larger air mass of 1,036 millibars which is currently in the Pacific and which could pass through Brazil during the week of July 7.
Given the size of the air mass, it may present the greatest frost threat seen so far this year should it reach coffee regions, Custodio said.
